description: Kilo is the all-in-one agentic engineering platform. Build, ship, and iterate faster with the most popular open source coding agent.
vibe: Ship fast, name short, never swallow an error, and let the typechecker do the talking.
highlights: Mandatory single-word naming for agent-written code, with explicit good/bad examples like `pid`, `cfg`, `err` versus `inputPID`, `existingClient`, `connectTimeout`.
Hard ban on empty catch blocks, with a three-step decision tree: remove the try/catch, handle explicitly, or at minimum log via `log.error`.
Style rules that eliminate whole classes of bugs: no `let` unless reassigning, no `else` after early return, no `any`, no out-of-bounds indexing (`array.at(-1)` over `array[array.length - 1]`).
CI-enforced guardrails for a fork: `kilocode_change` markers, workflow allowlist, source-link extraction, and an Effect facade ratchet to prevent upstream merge drift.
Explicit quality-check matrix per package, plus the blunt rule that root `bun test` is forbidden and exits with code 1.
assessment: This file reads like a senior maintainer who has been burned by merge conflicts, silent failures, and verbose agent output. The naming and style rules are unusually opinionated but internally consistent: short names, no `let`, no `else`, no empty catches all reduce surface area for bugs and review noise. The CI guardrails around `kilocode_change` markers and workflow allowlists show real operational maturity for a large fork, treating upstream drift as a first-class engineering problem rather than an afterthought.
